title: Period end: the question after a fresh check-in, nothing rolling on silently, and "to decide"
written_in: SCHEMA_V3 7.4, 9; DECISIONS_ROUND2 A7, F8, H8, L (period end q1 to q10), M6, M7, N5; DECISIONS.md (money left at month end never drops out silently, 18 Nov)
notes: Every amount is made up and in whole minor units (yen).
A period runs from the day the period stream's pay lands to the day before the next one lands [F8]. While the next pay has not landed (late, H8) the period has not ended.
The last 3 days of a period are its last day and the two days before it.

Question `question_start`: has the period ended, its last day, and whether the period-end question has to start with a check-in; while pay is past its posting window, `askPayCame` [L period_end q3]. A check-in is a date (every account typed) or `{ date, accounts }`; `spendFrom` lists the spend-from accounts [L period_end q9], and the check-ins of the last 3 days count together [M6]. `events` may hold the saved `{ k: 'periodStart', date }` event of a new period the person started without the pay [N5]: a live one (no `gone`) dated after `periodFrom` and on or before today starts the new period on its date, the old period ends the day before, and `pay` says whether the late pay is still "late, expected" (inside its posting window) or "not seen yet" [M7]. Question `leftovers`: for each place, what is decided (moved), what is kept in the place, what is still "to decide", how much an overspent place is over and what covers it, and the `move` events the answers write; answers adding up to more than is left are refused [L period_end q4, q6, q10]. Question `screen`: whether the period-end question is shown [L period_end q5]. Question `next_period`: what each place holds in the new period and how much of it counts in safe to spend [L period_end q6, q7]. Question `leftovers_ends`: two or more unanswered period ends, each answered on its own [L period_end q8].

An answer is `{ place, to, a, told }` (a move to another place), `{ place, keep: true, a, told }` (keep it here) or, for an overspent place, `{ place, from, a, told }` where `from` is `free` or `waiting` (what covers it).

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: A check-in in the last 3 days: the question starts straight away
cases.why: The next pay landed Thu 10 Dec, so the period ran 10 Nov to Wed 9 Dec [F8]. Its last 3 days are 7, 8 and 9 Dec. The check-in on 8 Dec is one of them, so it is fresh and the question needs no new check-in [A7].

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: The last check-in is the day before the last 3 days: the question starts with a check-in
cases.why: Last 3 days: 7 to 9 Dec. The newest check-in, 6 Dec, is before them, so Free to spend may still hold spending nobody entered (sweep2_experience 7). A7: the question starts with the check-in.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: A check-in on the first of the last 3 days counts
cases.why: 7 Dec is the first of the last 3 days (7, 8, 9), so it is inside them. Asked on 11 Dec, a day later; the question still needs no new check-in.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: A check-in on the period's last day counts
cases.why: 9 Dec is the period's last day, the third of its last 3 days.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: Pay lands two days early: the period ends early and so do its last 3 days
cases.why: Pay due 10 Dec landed Tue 8 Dec, which starts the new period [F8]. The old one ends Mon 7 Dec; its last 3 days are 5, 6 and 7 Dec. The check-in on 6 Dec is inside them.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: Pay is late: the period has not ended, nothing is asked
cases.why: Pay due Thu 10 Dec has not landed on Fri 11 Dec. While pay is late the period does not move on [H8], so there is no period end yet and no question. Fri 11 Dec is the last day of its posting window (Thu 10 + 1 working day), so the check-in does not ask about the pay yet (after it, pe-16) [L period_end q3].

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: In the middle of a period nothing is asked
cases.why: The next pay is due 10 Dec; on 25 Nov it has not landed and is not due, so the period is still running.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: Pay every two weeks: a short period, the same 3 days
cases.why: The period ran Fri 13 Nov to Thu 26 Nov. Last 3 days: 24, 25, 26 Nov. The check-in on 23 Nov is one day too early, so the question starts with a check-in.

cases.question: leftovers
cases.title: Free to spend has money left and nothing is answered yet: it waits, to decide
cases.why: 12,000 is left in Free to spend. Nothing rolls on silently [A7]: it stays in Free to spend, marked to decide, and no event moves it until the person answers.

cases.question: leftovers
cases.title: A budget line with money left waits too; one with nothing left has nothing to decide
cases.why: A7 covers Free to spend and every budget line: food's 3,000 waits, to decide. Free to spend ended at exactly 0, so there is no money to place. (When nothing is left anywhere, the screen shows one line and asks nothing, pe-24 [L period_end q5].)

cases.question: leftovers
cases.title: An answer given three days late is a move dated the period's last day
cases.why: 7.4: answers are move events dated the period's last day, 9 Dec, even when answered on 12 Dec. The move's `told` is when it was answered (section 0: told is when the app heard of it). All 12,000 is placed, nothing waits.

cases.question: leftovers
cases.title: A part answer: the rest still waits, to decide
cases.why: 5,000 is answered (a move to the trip, dated 9 Dec). 12,000 - 5,000 = 7,000 has no answer, so it waits in Free to spend, to decide, until answered [A7].

cases.question: leftovers
cases.title: One place split between two answers
cases.why: 5,000 + 7,000 = 12,000, all of it. Two move events, both dated 9 Dec. Nothing waits.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: A check-in the day after pay counts: the question needs no new one
cases.why: The period ran to Wed 9 Dec. The check-in on 11 Dec is after the end; it counts [L period_end q1], and its stretch (7 to 11 Dec) is split by days at the 10 Dec pay: 3 days to the old period, 2 to the new (A4). So the question starts straight away.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: On the period's last day, after a check-in, nothing is asked until pay is seen
cases.why: The question comes when the next period-starting pay is seen [L period_end q2]. On Wed 9 Dec the 10 Dec pay has not landed, so the period has not ended, even with a check-in that day.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: Pay past its posting window: the period waits and the check-in asks "did your pay come?"
cases.why: Pay due Thu 10 Dec, window Thu 10 + 1 working day = Fri 11. On Mon 14 it is past the window and not seen. The period waits for pay; the check-in asks "did your pay come?" [L period_end q3].

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: The person says the pay came on Fri 11: the period ends the day before
cases.why: Answering "yes, on Fri 11" writes the pay landed 11 Dec, which starts the new period [L period_end q3, F8]. The old one ends Thu 10 Dec; its last 3 days are 8, 9 and 10 Dec, and the 8 Dec check-in is one of them.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: A check-in that typed only the bank, not the cash: not fresh
cases.why: A check-in is fresh only when every spend-from account was typed [L period_end q9]. The 8 Dec check-in is in the last 3 days but typed only the bank; the cash was not counted, so the question starts with a check-in.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: A check-in that typed every spend-from account: fresh
cases.why: The 8 Dec check-in typed the bank and the cash, both spend-from accounts, and is in the last 3 days (7 to 9 Dec), so it is fresh [L period_end q9].

cases.question: leftovers
cases.title: An overspent line is shown with how much it is over, not yet covered
cases.why: Food ended at -3,000: it is shown with how much it is over, 3,000, to be covered from what is left in Free to spend, then Waiting, as the person picks [L period_end q4]. Nothing is answered yet: 3,000 to cover, and Free to spend's 12,000 waits, to decide.

cases.question: leftovers
cases.title: The overspend covered from Free to spend: a move, and less left to decide
cases.why: The person covers food's 3,000 from Free to spend [L period_end q4]: a move of 3,000 from free to food dated the period's last day (7.4). Free to spend: 12,000 - 3,000 = 9,000 still to decide.

cases.question: leftovers
cases.title: Free to spend has too little: the rest of the overspend from Waiting
cases.why: Free to spend has 2,000 left, all of it moved to food; the other 1,000 comes from Waiting [L period_end q4]: 2,000 + 1,000 = 3,000 covered. Free to spend has nothing left to decide.

cases.question: leftovers
cases.title: "Keep it here": no move, the money stays in its place, decided
cases.why: "Keep it here" leaves 5,000 in Free to spend with no move [L period_end q6]. 12,000 - 5,000 = 7,000 still waits, to decide.

cases.question: screen
cases.title: Nothing left anywhere: one line, no question
cases.why: Food and Free to spend both ended at 0. With nothing left the screen shows one line, "nothing left this time", and asks no question [L period_end q5].

cases.question: screen
cases.title: Money left in one place: the question is shown
cases.why: Free to spend has 12,000 left, so the question is shown (always asked, Mako decision 3); only when nothing is left is it one line [L period_end q5].

cases.question: next_period
cases.title: Kept money adds on top; money to decide is not in safe to spend
cases.why: The new period gives Free to spend 80,000. The 5,000 kept adds on top [L period_end q6]: 80,000 + 5,000 = 85,000 counts. The 7,000 still to decide stays in the place but is not in the new period's safe to spend [L period_end q7]. Held: 80,000 + 5,000 + 7,000 = 92,000.

cases.question: leftovers_ends
cases.title: Two unanswered period ends stay apart; a late answer takes its own period's last day
cases.why: The December and January ends were both left unanswered. They stay apart, each answered with its own last day [L period_end q8]: the December answer, given on 9 Jan, moves 12,000 dated 9 Dec; January's 8,000 still waits, to decide.

cases.question: leftovers
cases.title: Answers adding up to more than is left are refused, with the amount left
cases.why: 8,000 + 5,000 = 13,000, more than the 12,000 left. The answers are refused and the screen shows the 12,000 left [L period_end q10].

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: The bank typed on 7 Dec, the cash on 8 Dec: together they are fresh
cases.why: The period ran to Wed 9 Dec; its last 3 days are 7, 8 and 9 Dec. "Fresh" counts the check-ins of the last 3 days together [M6]: 7 Dec typed the bank and 8 Dec the cash, so between them every spend-from account was typed, and the question needs no new check-in. Before M6 each check-in had to type both.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: The bank typed on 6 Dec, the cash on 8 Dec: the bank is not in the last 3 days
cases.why: Last 3 days: 7 to 9 Dec. Only the 8 Dec check-in is inside them, and it typed only the cash [M6]. The bank was last typed on 6 Dec, before them, so the question starts with a check-in.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: Pay not seen, the person starts the new period on Mon 14 Dec: the old one ends Sun 13, the pay is not seen yet
cases.why: A new period started without the pay is saved as an event `{ k: 'periodStart', date }` [N5] and starts on its date, the day the person chose, Mon 14 Dec, so the old one ends Sun 13 Dec [M7]. Its last 3 days are 11, 12 and 13 Dec, and the 12 Dec check-in is one of them. The pay due Thu 10 Dec has a window to Fri 11 (Thu 10 + 1 working day); on Mon 14 that is over, so the pay is "not seen yet" [M7, H8].

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: The same start while the pay's window is still open: the pay stays expected
cases.why: The period ends Sun 13 Dec as in pe-31 [M7]. This account's window is 3 working days: Thu 10 Dec + Fri 11, Mon 14, Tue 15. On Mon 14 the window has not ended, so the late pay stays expected [M7, H8].

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: Two days later the window is over: the late pay is not seen yet
cases.why: The window ended Tue 15 Dec (pe-32). On Wed 16 it is over and the pay has not landed, so it is "not seen yet" [M7]. The period still ended on Sun 13, the day before the start the person chose.

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: A `periodStart` that was undone starts nothing: the check-in asks "did your pay come?"
cases.why: The `periodStart` event has `gone` (Undo, section 0), so no period was started [N5]. The pay due Thu 10 Dec has not landed and its window ended Fri 11, so on Mon 14 the period has not ended and the check-in asks "did your pay come?" [L period_end q3].

cases.question: question_start
cases.title: A `periodStart` on or before this period's first day belongs to an earlier period
cases.why: This period started on 10 Nov, from the `periodStart` dated 10 Nov [N5]; that event is what began it, so it does not end it. The pay due Thu 10 Dec has not landed, and on Thu 10 Dec its window (to Fri 11) is open, so the period has not ended and nothing is asked yet [H8, L period_end q2].

cases.question: leftovers_merged
cases.title: Both phones answer the period end the same way: one answer, 20,000 moved once
cases.why: Each phone writes its answer as `pe:2026-12-24:free` [O2], so the merge keeps one record (newest `at`, earliest `told`, 09:00). 20,000 leaves Free to spend once; before O2 the merged copy moved 40,000 out of a place that held 20,000 (final_review_1 S4).

cases.question: leftovers_merged
cases.title: Answers that each phone allowed are refused together after the merge
cases.why: Jun's phone moves all 20,000 of Free to spend to the trip; Tess's phone covers Food's 5,000 overspend from Free to spend. Each alone is fine (20,000 and 5,000 of 20,000). They are different records (`pe:2026-12-24:free`, `pe:2026-12-24:food`), so both survive the merge; checked again after it [O2], Free to spend gives 20,000 + 5,000 = 25,000 of 20,000, which is refused, the amount left shown [L period_end q10].

cases.question: found_later
cases.title: An old statement read after the answer: the answer stays, the overspend is found later
cases.why: At the answer Free to spend had 20,000 left and all of it went to the trip. A statement read later adds 30,000 of spending dated in that period: 20,000 - 30,000 = -10,000 really left. The answer stays [O]; the place is now 20,000 - (-10,000) = 30,000 short, shown at the next check-in as found later.

cases.question: found_later
cases.title: A later statement that fits in what still waits to decide: no overspend
cases.why: 5,000 went to the trip and 15,000 waited to decide. The later 10,000 comes out of the money still in the place: 20,000 - 10,000 = 10,000 really left, 5,000 given, 10,000 - 5,000 = 5,000 still to decide. Nothing is overspent, so nothing is found later; the answer stays [O].
